Spec amendments: 2 need your call - from the spec review; applying as recommended reopens no tasks; no phase change.

1. Share retry policy - move retry policy into one owner. Adapters currently disagree about when to retry: the alpha adapter retries twice and the beta adapter four times.
   Changing who owns retry policy is an architecture choice, so it needs your decision.
   Example: adapter-local retry limits -> one coordinator retry limit
   Reviewer: changing retry ownership needs a human architecture choice
   Impact: Design / retries: each report adapter decides its own retries -> one shared owner decides retries for every adapter
   A) accept - a new retry service owns all retry policies
   B) alt-1 - the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy, and adapters keep execution
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: B - the existing coordinator keeps policy consistent without adding a new service

2. Classify blocked execution - classify exit 126 as blocked rather than failed. Operators need to tell a launch problem apart from a report failure, and the launch test returns 126 before the report runs.
   This changes a status that operators see, so it needs your decision.
   Example: exit 126 = failed -> blocked
   Reviewer: operator-visible status changes need a human decision
   Impact: Design / run status: a run that exits 126 is reported as failed -> it is reported as blocked
   A) accept - exit 126 is blocked
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: A - a separate status identifies launch failures

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details
crosscut: Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: a new retry service owns all retry policies (alt-1 new: the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy; adapters keep execution)
exit126: Design / run status - old: exit 126 is failed -> new: exit 126 is blocked
